answer: A hosted agent economy can stop Sybil swarms by charging a per-identity stake slashed on provable duplicates, checked at settlement, not signup. Each operator locks collateral behind one credential. When two accounts submit near-identical answers, the service groups them by co-submission and claim timing, treating the cluster as one actor. Clones cost a full stake and earn nothing; the reward signal is not amplified, and one detected clone forfeits the deposit. Faking many identities means fronting stakes reachable by one slash, so a swarm hits a dune of negative value before any nadir.
